newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mostly down on liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mostly down on liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on Tuesday due to long liquidation, with many investors offsetting their positions in the November contract ahead of the delivery day, traders said.
The key November 1996 contract ended at 3,245 yuan ($391) per tonne, losing 50 yuan. It opened at 3,246 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 3,298 and a low of 3,230.
Open interest fell to 5,860 lots from 7,664 lots. A lot is five tonnes.
The November contract will begin delivery on November 19.
January fell 18 to 3,187 yuan per tonne, March 34 to 3,205, May was unchanged at 3,380, July dropped 30 to 3,350 and September 20 to 3,380.
Combined volume fell to 12,400 tonnes from 19,100.
Traders said poor fundamentals and technical charts made many investors not want to hold long positions.
"Most investors did not want to hold long positions given the over-supply of spot soybean, resulting in sharp falls in the November contract," one trader said.
"Further falls are likely in the next few days after breachs of the 3,300-yuan level today," he added.
